PART II
Task & Modality Structure
Fig. 5 · Task × Modality
Task Composition within Each Data Modality
100% stacked bar showing primary task breakdown per data modality (n = 60). Multi-task resources dominate radiology and sensor data; EHR/clinical text covers the broadest range of single tasks.
Fig. 6 · NLP Tasks
Primary NLP Task Distribution
Primary task category per dataset, following the task classification criteria; datasets annotated for more than one task are grouped as "Multiple tasks" (n = 60)
Fig. 7 · Sankey
Task → Modality → Annotation Granularity
Flow diagram showing how dataset NLP tasks (left) map to data modalities (center) and annotation granularity levels (right). Width of each band is proportional to number of datasets (n = 60).
PART III
Language & Coverage
Fig. 8 · Language
Language Coverage
53 datasets (88.3%) are English only; 7 (11.7%) are multilingual or non-English, exposing a multilingual gap in clinical NLP (n = 60)
PART IV
FAIR-Aligned Metadata Completeness
Fig. 9 · FAIR Heatmap
FAIR-Aligned Metadata Completeness (Dataset × Field)
60 datasets (rows, sorted by overall score ↓) × 16 metadata fields (columns, four per FAIR dimension). Each field is scored with the predefined FAIR-aligned scoring rubric (Appendix 3) on five levels; undocumented or not-applicable fields score 0. The overall score is the mean of the 16 field scores. Dimension means: Findable 0.89, Accessible 0.83, Interoperable 0.72, Reusable 0.52; overall mean 0.74. Scores reflect documentation completeness, not dataset quality. Hover for details.
